content: The Baduy (Kanekes) are a Sundanese adat community in western Java, ~11,000 people. Divided into Baduy Dalam (Inner Baduy, ~1,200, strict adherence — no electricity, motorised transport, cameras, soap, or synthetic cloth) and Baduy Luar (Outer Baduy, more flexible). Visitors may enter Baduy Luar with a local guide; Baduy Dalam entry requires the guide's introduction and strict rule observance (no photos of people, no ATM/mobile use during the visit, respect for pikukuh customary law). Access: Ciboleger village, ~4 hours from Jakarta.

The Toraja are a highland South Sulawesi adat community (~1M people) organised around Aluk Todolo (their pre-Christian religion — now a recognised penghayat kepercayaan) alongside Protestant Christianity. Most famous for rambu solo' (elaborate multi-day funeral rites) and tongkonan (boat-shaped ancestral houses). Visitors are welcome at funerals as respectful guests; customary gifts (cigarettes, sugar, palm wine) are appropriate. Do not photograph without asking; wear dark colours; expect emotional intensity.

The Dayak Iban are one of many Dayak subgroups spread across Kalimantan (Borneo). Traditional longhouse (rumah betang / rumah panjai) communities on major rivers. Aluk Todolo-like animist beliefs coexist with Christianity, with adat law regulating land, marriage, and dispute. Visiting a longhouse: approach through the tuai rumah (headman), remove shoes, accept offered tuak (rice wine) with the right hand (a small sip is respectful — full refusal can be rude).

Sade village (Rembitan, central Lombok) is a Sasak adat village widely opened to respectful tourism — thatched-roof lumbung (rice barn) houses, weaving demonstrations, and preserved marriage-by-elopement (kawin lari) tradition. Entry: donation to the community box (~30k IDR fair). Local guides offered — negotiate before starting. Do not enter houses uninvited. The nearby Ende village is a quieter alternative less on the tour circuit.

The Mentawai people live on the Mentawai Islands off West Sumatra's coast — culturally + linguistically distinct from mainland Minangkabau. Known for sikerei (shamans), extensive body tattooing (titi), sharpened teeth traditions (increasingly rare), and Arat Sabulungan animist religion (now a recognised penghayat kepercayaan). Deep-interior visits (Siberut) require multi-day trekking + local guide; respectful visits arranged through community-based tourism operators.
